chunks: From him, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Jarrah al-Madaini, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:
Regarding the man who returns (revokes) his charity, he said: 'He is like the one who returns what he vomited.'

key_terms.يَرْتَدُّ: returns or revokes (specifically in the context of taking back a gift or charity)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on revoking a gift or charity after giving it?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the legal ruling on revoking a gift (*hibah*) by comparing it to a person who vomits and then eats it again, highlighting the repulsiveness and futility of the act. This analogy underscores the spiritual and social awkwardness of retracting charity, a concept deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence regarding the finality of gifts once given. The comparison serves not only as a legal precedent but also as a moral lesson on the sincerity and permanence of charitable giving.
